deals.headline: Sevilla borrows EUR 108m from Goldman Sachs
deals.summary: Sevilla FC took a EUR 108m loan from Goldman Sachs in 2024, which it extended by EUR 70m in December 2025.

deals.evidence: la ejecución del suplemento del crédito que firmó con Goldman Sachs de 70 millones de euros más sobre el original de 108 millones
deals.headline: Goldman Sachs loan topped up by EUR 70m to EUR 178m
deals.summary: Ahead of the December 2025 AGM the board presented a EUR 70m supplement to its EUR 108m Goldman Sachs loan, taking it to EUR 178m, to cover deferred Covid-era tax payments falling due in 2026.

deals.evidence: el aproximadamente 15 por ciento del capital social del Sevilla FC que tenía 777 partners pasa a tener como dueño a la aseguradora
deals.headline: Insurer A-CAP takes 777 Partners' stake of about 15% in Sevilla after an auction
deals.summary: After 777 Partners collapsed, the Sevilla FC shares it held through Sevillistas Unidos 2020 (about 15% per ABC; about 14% per IUSPORT and Diario de Sevilla) went to auction and were taken over by the insurer A-CAP, which had custody of them. A-CAP's votes have backed the current board.

name: Sevilla Fútbol Club, S.A.D.
notes: Revenue is net turnover for the year to 30 June 2025 (EUR 115.18m; the club's 2024-25 annual report table gives EUR 115,185 thousand, down from EUR 174,970 thousand), and the net result was a EUR 54.06m loss with negative equity of EUR 123.5m at 30 June 2025. The audited financial statements in the club's PDF are scanned images, so pre-tax result, wages and a revenue breakdown were not taken from them. Press stakes overlap: Palco23 says the five families own 85% together, while Diario de Sevilla and IUSPORT put A-CAP's package at about 14%, and Relevo (2023) said nobody could pin down each bloc's current percentage, so the family rows carry no stake. The EUR 450m valuation is the price agreed in May 2026 (including debt) for a deal that collapsed; RMG's EUR 420m bid was rejected in August 2026, and on 1 October 2026 ABC reported that the families still intended to sell, with the process in the hands of Goldman Sachs, also the club's largest creditor. Net debt (EUR 88m at 31 December 2025) is the club's own figure, which bidders dispute. Midea's shirt deal ended on 30 June 2026, and Forbes España (10 August 2026) listed Sevilla without a front-of-shirt sponsor for 2026-27. Social-media counts and a Forbes, Deloitte or KPMG valuation were not found for the club.

ownership_summary: Sevilla Fútbol Club, S.A.D. is controlled by five local family blocs: Del Nido (José María del Nido Benavente is the largest individual shareholder; his son José María del Nido Carrasco is president), Castro (the Utrera group's Sevillistas de Nervión S.A.), Carrión, Alés and Guijarro. They are bound by a governance pact signed in November 2019 that runs to the end of 2027, and Palco23 reports that together they own 85%. The US insurer A-CAP holds about 14%, taken over at auction in June 2025 from 777 Partners' vehicle Sevillistas Unidos 2020; the rest is spread across many small shareholders. A May 2026 deal to sell about 80% to Sergio Ramos and Five Eleven Capital, valuing the club at about EUR 450m including debt, collapsed. Goldman Sachs was hired in July 2026 to find a buyer, and in August 2026 the families rejected a EUR 420m offer from Riverside Management Group.
